reasoning: Preserved all three failure-driven edits. Consolidated the overlapping option-audit insight into the non-protected failure edit, making its procedure apply to every option and explicitly rank supported claims. Kept the distinct counterexample and formula-verification checks. Excluded the success edit targeting the protected section; its option-selection insight is covered without editing that section.

edits.target: - Compare logical strength under the hypotheses and choose the strongest claim actually established. Do not settle for a weaker consequence when an exact or strongest result is requested, but do not add an unsupported converse, endpoint, equality, exception, or other strengthening. Retain any condition on a valid conditional conclusion rather than silently assuming it holds.
edits.content: For every option, especially near-duplicates, audit the full claim clause by clause—not just its shared core—and mark each conjunct, condition, converse, and added conclusion as supported or unsupported by the established result. Note what the requested claim requires that the option omits; reject options containing unsupported clauses, then rank the remaining supported options against the requested strength rather than stopping at a true but weaker consequence. For an exact classification, require both directions.

edits.target: - Check distinctions such as universal claims versus claims about a special subclass or extendible objects; restricted-range versus full-range claims; local versus global results; eventual versus finite-time behavior; and interior-time versus endpoint regularity. Extra rates, coefficients, and other precise details require their own support.
edits.content: If an option gives a result on a restricted parameter range and also asserts a counterexample outside that range, verify the two clauses separately. Independently establish the alleged existential counterexample; a theorem covering only the restricted range does not show failure beyond it.

edits.target: - For exact identities and formulas, check signs, coefficients, and term or index order; resemblance or asymptotic agreement does not establish equality.
edits.content: When choices differ by a small symbolic change, independently derive or verify the disputed expression from the definitions or theorem, especially for shifted exponents and asymptotic powers. Check indices, integer factors or divisibility, and which parameter or coefficient belongs to each term; do not rely on resemblance to a remembered formula.
